title: Routing regex regression: an unmerged patch yields to documented API boundaries and explicit workarounds

boundary_decision.rationale: All ten increments concern the same routing contract: whether path strings may contain general regex, whether the proposed optional-question-mark patch should restore that behavior, and which supported alternatives cover the affected use cases.
boundary_decision.falsification: Split the case only if an audited source shows that wildcard SPA routing and slash/no-slash routing were maintained as independent decisions with no shared regex-escaping or public-API premise.

excluded_sources.reason: Only repeats the already visible Issue-to-PR relationship.
Restates that regex behavior was undocumented and adds a civility request, but no new technical constraint or decision.
The revert/version/docs proposal is quoted by the immediately following included maintainer response, which is the actual decision-state change.
Adds external provenance for the old workaround and repeats the documentation concern without changing the repository decision.
The TestClient redirect debugging branch is inconclusive and tangential; it ends in a reproduction correction rather than a durable STR-07 routing decision.
Post-scope acknowledgement repeats that the dual-route workaround is useful but adds no new boundary.
A later third-party regex monkey patch occurs after the registered decision window and relies on the rejected implementation surface.
Mention, subscription, cross-reference, and head-ref deletion events add no task-relevant state.

source_body_history_limitations: GitHub does not expose complete immutable edit history for Issue/PR bodies through the normal API. Current body SHA-256 and source_updated_at values are change detectors; creation summaries are limited to immutable title, timestamped comments, the initial commit, and the observed patch.
